headline: High-risk filesystem and network interaction: OpenHands can write, execute, and exfiltrate while langchain4j has no isolation or I/O surfaces documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenHands can use MCP, browsers, and files in its runtime, so if langchain4j outputs are passed into its prompts or tools, instruction-like content could be misread. langchain4j documents no I/O surfaces or isolation, so the bridge is plausible but not proven. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF langchain4j output is copied into OpenHands prompts or MCP inputs
IF OpenHands treats file or web content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of model outputs into OpenHands prompts
Add a provenance tag to all langchain4j outputs
Require a human review step before MCP actions
Restrict OpenHands to trusted local files only
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-separation guards

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenHands reads and writes files in its runtime and has broad network egress, while langchain4j documents no network egress and no data classes touched. If both share mounted files, OpenHands can ingest those files and transmit their contents externally. The shared-workspace path is plausible from the profiles, but the exact data flow is not directly documented.
conditions: IF both agents access the same mounted files
IF sensitive files are present in OpenHands' runtime sandbox
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different volumes
Remove secrets from any shared mount
Set OpenHands network egress to allowlist-only
Rotate any credentials exposed in shared files
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenHands can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; langchain4j has no write or coordination controls documented. If both operate on the same repo or mounted directory, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide and corrupt state. Because OpenHands defaults include these write capabilities and no locking is shown, the conflict risk is high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git repository
IF no external lock or queue serializes their actions
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent during the other's write phase
Use a file lock around git operations
Limit OpenHands to read-only mode for shared repos
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutual exclusion

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenHands can act on files, browsers, and shell commands, so if it consumes langchain4j-generated text as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions. langchain4j is a library with no documented verification or action gating, so the handoff is unverified. The pathway exists in default OpenHands-style agent loops, but the blast radius is not clearly irreversible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF OpenHands uses langchain4j output as a source of facts or instructions
IF OpenHands executes shell or browser actions based on that output
mitigations: Require a verification step before actions
Mark langchain4j output as untrusted by default
Constrain OpenHands to dry-run mode for critical tasks
Add citation checks before execution
requires-engineering: implement structured validation of agent outputs

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for langchain4j, while OpenHands handles files in a Docker runtime and model-provider API keys. The profiles do not show regulated data classes or a cross-border policy conflict, so only a small compliance gap is plausible. I do not cite both agents here because the issue is a lack of documented mismatch, not a proven shared-data pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into OpenHands runtime files
IF the configured model provider stores prompts outside the operator's required jurisdiction
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the runtime
Review the model provider's retention settings
Use a jurisdiction-approved provider
Delete runtime files after use
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
